initial:
Create one large landscape paired front/back review mockup for PulseSensor, using the three images in order.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: verified RC3 B JST board CIRCUIT/BACK face, all actual parts positions are locked.
Image 2 is the EDIT TARGET: same RC3 B OPTICAL/FRONT face, sensor and light aperture positions locked.
Image 3 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: earlier PulseSensor heart/website face. Do not import its electrical geometry.
Output two equal large orthographic boards side by side, optical/front on LEFT and circuit/back on RIGHT, with generous margin. White neutral backdrop, clear black text labels outside boards 'OPTICAL / FRONT' and 'CIRCUIT / BACK', header 'PulseSensor · appearance study', footer 'VISUAL CONCEPT — NOT FABRICATION ARTWORK'. Black solder mask and white graphics on both faces. Preserve ALL component bodies, pads, vias, traces, outline, exact placement, scale and connector access from images 1 and 2. Never move or replace components to make room.
LEFT: translate only the visual identity from image 3: broad white heart, black field, clean curved lowercase 'pulsesensor.com' along lower arc. Adapt heart cutouts around original image 2 optical detector and LED lens, keep both optically unobstructed by ink, do not move detector or lens. This is a best-match reconstruction, not exact original master artwork. Render URL upright and readable along arc.
RIGHT: elegant restrained white educational silkscreen overlay in remaining empty spaces of image1; a beginner circuit-function illustration. Avoid long text, tiny paragraphs, boxes crossing component bodies, component relocation, or colored graphics. Suggested compact distinct callouts 'SENSE', 'FILTER', 'AMP', 'OUT', 'LED', 'POWER'. Use delicate dashed conceptual arrows in open lanes and small simple icons where room permits. Functional story is optical sensor on OTHER SIDE -> filter network -> amplifier -> JST signal output. LED is a separate illumination branch, power separate supply; do NOT draw LED as a serial stage in the sensor signal path, do NOT call the op amp a transimpedance amplifier. Avoid presenting arrows as literal copper traces.
Exact board reference: image1 has U2 amplifier top center, D1 LED middle, JST at bottom center; filter capacitors distributed left and bottom-right, with final filter/gain region upper-right. Only mark SENSE as 'SENSE' with a tiny return-side cue near lower-center outside connector keepout, rather than invent a sensor body on back. Do not add pin numbering or pin-order labels in this concept. Keep major existing objects and their complete geometry visually identical. Concept must look like a plausible tiny real PCB with minimal white silkscreen, not an infographic pasted over the parts. No new electronics. All new drawing is cosmetic ink.
revision:
Edit the attached PulseSensor paired appearance study. Keep the ENTIRE left optical/front view, titles, footer, and ALL physical board components on right unchanged. Correct ONLY white explanatory graphics on right. Current arrows incorrectly link sense, power, LED and output. Remove ALL right-board existing text, icons and dashed arrows, except keep original physical component outline/polarity markings.
Replace with a deliberately simple separate educational legend in free black gaps, without arrows that claim actual copper connections:
- '1 SENSE' at lower left open edge with tiny second line 'FRONT'
- '2 FILTER' in upper left open gap just beneath the top-left rim
- '3 AMP' above top-center amplifier
- '4 OUT' along right open edge, with one short dotted pointer ending at the right SIDE of the white JST connector, no pointer to a resistor.
- 'LED' beside the actual central white rectangular LED body, with a small sun icon, unconnected to the numbered stages.
Remove POWER label entirely and DO NOT connect LED to the numbered signal chain. No flow arrows between the numbered stages: ordered numbers convey functional order. Do not add new parts or move any existing component, do not replace a pad or via with text. Keep exact front heart, 'pulsesensor.com', and optical components. This is a minimal beginner legend, schematic-inspired but not a full schematic. Black and white only. No extra filter label, no arrows pointing from filter to LED or vice versa. Preserve footer VISUAL CONCEPT — NOT FABRICATION ARTWORK.
